- **Dedup** — repo-scoped search for copy-on-claim / file-reference-lifecycle returns only the parent thread #6966 and PR #7101, of which this card is the deliberate split-out; no duplicate dispatch entry.

**ACCEPT.** PR #7224, reviewed by the `domain:services` seat (#6021, session `session_015fkdTyGmMD5s8ZtEifvuGy`). Marking ready and queueing.

Verified against GitHub rather than the report: **15 files** — the `file-reference-lifecycle` pair (declared surface), one changeset, **one declared surface deviation** (`packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts`, +1 row) and 11 regenerated `content/docs/references/api/*.mdx` (mechanical union-count bumps from `gen:docs`; `check:docs` reports 231 generated files in sync). **26/26 check runs completed, all `success`** (Console Pin Gate conditionally skipped); ESLint `success` 03:10:32Z (carries the `check:error-code-casing` family), TypeScript Type Check `success` 03:18:29Z, Build Docs / Spec property liveness / Check Changeset all `success` — read by job conclusion.

**The lane's REFUSE ruling is implemented as ruled**, and its falsifiable premise was verified and NOT falsified: the dev swept every `multi: true` call site outside objectql and every declared file-class field name across packages/, examples/, qa/ and the docs corpus — no consumer depends on a predicate update writing a file-class field succeeding. Both PM mechanism assumptions held on measurement (per-row dispatch mode visible in beforeUpdate; throw propagates uncaught with `code`+`status` intact). Refusal is scoped by `isFileIdToken` — bulk clear, external URL, non-file fields keep working, each pinned; single-record/insert/delete byte-identical. Every refusal test asserts `code` + `status` (ADR-0112), which is load-bearing here exactly per the #6142 lesson: the pre-fix path doesn't throw at all, so throw-only assertions could not distinguish "refused with the wrong envelope" from "did not refuse".

**Surface deviation ruled JUSTIFIED**: minting `FILE_FIELD_BULK_WRITE_REFUSED` requires an `ERROR_CODE_LEDGER` row (ADR-0112 D3 — an unregistered code becomes a wire code by side effect), and the alternative (reusing `INVALID_REQUEST`) is the exact anti-pattern the ledger header warns against. This is a producer-side registry entry the ruled fix requires, not a consumer patched to dodge the refusal — the #5586 shape, declared loudly in the PR body. Per the #6532 precedent this seat is posting a cross-seat declaration on the `domain:spec` seat card, since `packages/spec` is hard-owned there.
